speaker: Doctor
text: You mentioned an episode of upper abdominal pain three years ago; did you receive any diagnosis or imaging results from that event? I also need to know if you have experienced any unintended weight loss or changes in your bowel habits since that time.

speaker: Patient
text: has abstained from alcohol for these three years, after having consumed 1–2 beers daily for 40 years. He has a 50-year history of smoking a pack of cigarettes daily.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of smoking and the presence of painless jaundice with weight loss, I am concerned about a pancreatic malignancy obstructing the bile duct. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal CT Scan.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the CT scan was normal, I need to rule out other causes of obstructive jaundice. Do you have a history of gallstones or previous episodes of jaundice?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Episode of acute upper abdominal pain treated three years ago. History of long-term alcohol consumption and smoking. Social history: Stopped alcohol consumption three years ago; 50-year history of smoking a pack of cigarettes daily.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the obstructive symptoms and normal CT, I must evaluate the biliary tree directly. REQUEST TEST: MRCP.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRCP demonstrates a cystic dilatation of the extrahepatic bile duct with upstream dilation of the intrahepatic ducts. No obstructing mass or stone is identified within the visualized biliary tree. The findings are consistent with a choledochal cyst.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRCP findings of a cystic dilatation of the extrahepatic bile duct are diagnostic. DIAGNOSIS READY: Choledochal Cyst
